Domestic Energy

The domestic design is the KEPCO's APR+1550 advanced pressurized water nuclear reactor design. This design boasts more sophisticated reactor and safety features than it's predecessor the APR-1400. Each reactor would provide a capacity of 1550 MW by utilizing 257 fuel assemblies. The reactor would also feature 4 redundant safety backup generators to increase reliability and safety ratings that far surpass previous Korean designs. These reactors have been chosen for the latest generation of South Korean nuclear power plants expected to soon begin construction.

These new APR+1550 and the previous APR-1400 reactors are also being advertised for export to nations interested in expanding their nuclear power systems.

Merchant Ship Energy

Many of the world's ships use a highly pollutive fuel source known as bunker fuel. Other current designs for LNG tankers have utilized the very fuel being shipped in order to provide power. In order to reduce the amount of CO2 and pollutants released by the world's shipping lines, a think tank of South Korean and Dutch shipbuilding and energy companies have begun investigating whether or not there could be a commercially viable system to offer a solution. The designs would allow ships to use a variety of solar, wind, and nuclear energy sources to provide propulsion and power to the ship's various systems instead of fossil fuel sources. Among the designs are solar panel arrays, wind turbines, nuclear reactors, and even large sails, utilizing one of the oldest methods of ship propulsion. More details on the designs will be released as they're developed.
